newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Airways pilots end strike.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Airways pilots end strike.

text.p: Pilots at national carrier Kenya Airways on Thursday ended a two-day strike sparked by the suspension of two colleagues.

"Work will resume normally with immediate effect," the airline management and the pilots' union said in a joint statement issued by the labour and manpower development ministry, which negotiated an end to the strike action.

The pilots had called a strike from Wednesday to protest against the suspension of two of their colleagues. The statement said the suspensions would be deferred pending a ministry investigation into circumstances that led to the strike.
"All the affected pilots will continue to get their full pay pending the outcome of the ministry's investigations. There will be no victimisation by either party," the statement said.

Kenya Airways spokesman Koome Mwambia said the airline had informed the pilots' union that the strike action was in contravention of trade dispute laws that made it a criminal offence to strike without notice in an essential service.

"After the declaration of the strike on Wednesday, eight pilots reported sick, leading to the cancellation of (domestic) flights to Mombasa, Kisumu (and international flights to) Lilongwe, Lusaka and Dubai," Mwambia said earlier.
Kenya Airways employs some 110 pilots, Mwambia said.
The government sold 51 percent of its shareholding in the airline on the Nairobi Stock Exchange early this year.
That followed a government sale of a 26 percent stake in the airline to KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV. The stock was first traded on June 3.
Disputes between the airline and pilots have undermined the Kenya Airways share for some time now. From a flotation price of 11.25 shillings, it closed at 9.80 on Thursday.
In July, a court awarded the pilots around 411 million shillings representing two years' back pay after they complained they were some of the poorest paid pilots in the world.
